lines.text: A con man sold the Eiffel Tower. Twice.

parts.tts: A con man sold the Eiffel Tower. Twice.
parts.heard: A con man sold the Eiffel Tower...twice.

lines.text: In 1925, Victor Lustig forged government letterhead.

parts.tts: In nineteen twenty-five, Victor Lustig forged government letterhead.
parts.heard: In 1925, Victor Lustig forged government letterhead.

lines.text: He told 6 scrap dealers the tower was being torn down.

parts.tts: He told six scrap dealers the tower was being torn down.
parts.heard: He told six scrap dealers the tower was being torn down.

lines.text: Andre Poisson paid, plus a bribe. Lustig fled the country.

parts.tts: Andre Poisson paid, plus a bribe. Lustig fled the country.
parts.heard: Andre Poisson paid, plus a bribe. Lustig fled the country.

lines.text: Poisson was too embarrassed to call the cops.

parts.tts: Poisson was too embarrassed to call the cops.
parts.heard: Poisson was too embarrassed to call the cops.

lines.text: So Lustig came back, and reportedly sold it... AGAIN.

parts.tts: So Lustig came back, and reportedly sold it...
parts.heard: So Lustig came back and reportedly sold it.

lines.text: He did end up in Alcatraz. Not for the tower. For counterfeiting.
